title: Chick Webb's band after Ella Fitzgerald
summary: Dance and Caldwell consider Edgar Sampson versus Al Feldman and say Webb's band was a commercial group.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: That's a very funny thing, though, when you think -- so she -- Chick gets her, and that's great, isn't it? That's almost the end of his band. From then on that's just really just another -- and I know when I first came here, you know, he was with Gale, wasn't he, and I was just talking to some of them, and I was talking about Edgar Sampson's arrangements. And they say, no, you want to hear what this boy, Al Feldman, can do, you know, the guy that did, 'A Tisket, A Tasket.'
Yeah, Al Feldman, he's a good arranger.

-- what he could do, but I said, like what Edgar Sampson could do, and they argued with me. They said, oh, you're wrong. This man Al Feldman -- I mean he was just a hack compared to Sampson. But that suited what they did then.
That was a big hit. That sold it.
: But I mean that -- that was the end of the band as a band, wasn't it? And after that it --
After Chick died, that was it.
: Yeah. Well, I mean even before—
: -- you know, I mean there was Sandy and there was Bobby Stark there and Taft -- [Jordan]
: -- but there wasn't anything really happening. It was all over.
